notes:
Summary: SilverQuill builds an IDE-first copilot product embedded in VS Code and JetBrains IDEs. Primary goal for Redwood POC is to validate low-latency streaming + token-budget controls so inline completions feel instantaneous for developers. Key UX targets: TTFT (time-to-first-token) <= 80ms median for single-line completions, 95p jitter <= 40ms, graceful backpressure so editor doesn’t lock up under burst typing.

Recent feedback / observations:
- POC wired to hosted API; basic streaming works but TTFT currently ~120ms median on dev laptop -> not acceptable for pro product.
- Jitter spikes seen when agent sends many concurrent token streams (multiple buffer flushes). Suspect batching/backpressure policy and chunk size.
- Implemented session token budget (512 tokens) to limit long hallucinating generations; UX team wants dynamic budgets based on file context and user plan.
- Discussed model/version pinning: they want ability to pin a fast quantized variant for latency-sensitive lines and fall back to higher-quality model for larger snippets or summarization tasks.
- Security: enterprise customers require VPC + KMS + audit logs; SilverQuill wants Redwood Dedicated or Private for enterprise tier but open to hosted API for SMB users.
- Cost sensitivity: forecasted heavy token volume from active users; interested in Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization to save 25-40% token cost.

Quotes / snippets from calls:
- "If developers feel a lag while typing, they abandon the feature within a week." - CTO (call 2026-02-12)
- "We need a predictable upper bound on latency; occasional 200ms spikes are worse than consistent 120ms." - Lead UX PM

Technical action items / notes for Redwood team:
- Rafael to run A/B perf tests: websocket streaming with 16-token chunk vs 8-token chunk, measure TTFT and jitter. (status: in progress)
- Try model variant routing: pin quantized 4-bit variant for single-line completions; fallback to fp16 full model for multi-line generation. Capture cost delta and latency tradeoffs.
- Prototype server-side prefix caching for common repo imports to reduce KV cache warmup for short completions.
- Add backpressure tests: simulate 50 concurrent streams from one account to measure queueing and autoscaling response.
- Security: provide SOC2 summary and KMS integration doc to SilverQuill security (drive link above).

Next commercial steps:
- Deliver performance tuning workshop (on-site or remote) with SE + infra (target week of 2026-03-22).
- If POC TTFT improves to <=80ms median and jitter below 60ms 95p, SilverQuill moves to Dedicated evaluation and procurement discussion.

Short open questions / blockers to escalate:
- Can Redwood guarantee per-tenant network egress routing / region pinning for VPC Dedicated?
- Is there an easy knob for token-budget soft truncation vs hard stop that preserves streaming UX?
- Pricing model for high-volume short-completion workloads (many small tokens) vs long-form generations.
